issues.description: The gloss for the target word 'motorbike' — 'a bike that goes by itself, not by your legs' — is misleading. A motorbike does not go 'by itself'; it has an engine and needs a rider. 'By itself' suggests the vehicle moves on its own, which is not the defining feature. The intended contrast (engine power vs pedalling) should be stated directly.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the gloss to: 'a bicycle with an engine — you do not use your legs to make it go'.

qa_report.summary: All three dialogue lines are grammatically correct, natural and firmly A2, and they model the grammar point well: 'usually', 'always' and 'sometimes' all appear before the main verb, matching the (accurate) grammar note. Review words 'street' and 'morning' are recycled naturally, and the quiz-free micro-dialogue format is respected with a plausible 10-15 second length. The one real problem is the gloss for the target word 'motorbike': 'a bike that goes by itself' is misleading, since a motorbike has an engine and a rider — it does not move by itself. Fix that gloss and the episode is ready to record.
